summary: PASS. s14_windows_acl_recovery.rs (3 real-Win32 tests on tempdir targets + a real V1Store, all mutating real ACLs with best-effort restore) proves the full P14 matrix: prepared-shape journal discipline and the terminal Conflict state machine; the crash matrix (prepare-crash -> NothingApplied -> conflict 'never-applied'; apply-crash -> AlreadyApplied -> mark applied with the actual bytes -> byte-exact restore; external edit during prepared -> Conflict; external edit after readback -> restore refuses 'acl-changed-since-apply' and the foreign ACE survives) through real drop+reopen store restarts; physical-identity CAS refusal across targets; inherited-only child DACLs never faking a conflict while restore stays byte-CAS; and oldest-first target history whose journaled ActualAfter equals a fresh capture. Totals: Runtime 407/407 (401 baseline + 3 Engineer lib tests [lib 72->75] + 3 s14 — the task brief's '~404' assumed the Engineer's 3 were already inside 401; they were not, actual is 407), Kernel 75/75, Store 416/417 with only the declared plan_schema baseline, protocol+sdk 33/33, codex 13/13; cumulative 944/945/1. workspace --no-run/check/clippy -D warnings/fmt --check all green; quality_check ok with zero violations. Both documented mechanical deviations are judged justified and minimal: (1) services/sandbox.rs gains only the pre-declared #[cfg(windows)] pub mod windows; registration (6 lines incl. doc; without it the declared create cannot compile; P12 services/mod.rs precedent); (2) Cargo.toml adds exactly one windows-sys feature line Win32_Security_Authorization (GetSecurityInfo/SetSecurityInfo/SE_FILE_OBJECT live in that submodule; P15's isolation APIs remain untouched for their own task).
